title: Colour token layer for WCAG contrast certification
description:
Objective: give the control room resolvable colour values, so the spec's "Contrast >= WCAG AA" clause becomes measurable instead of unmeasurable.

WHY THIS EXISTS (project rail 4, Clause 2 gap measurement). Spec section 11.1 line 686 requires "Contrast >= WCAG AA". A contrast ratio needs two RESOLVED colours. At planning time the architect probed for any colour value on disk and found NONE:
- TruthSemanticTone is a PROSE union, not colour: packages/control-room-model/src/index.ts carries "neutral slate", "amber", "green", "blue", "high-contrast magenta" as semanticTone strings. Those name a colour; they are not one.
- Zero hex, rgb(), hsl() or oklch() literals exist in apps/control-room/src or in any packages/*/src.
- The repo contains exactly ONE stylesheet, apps/control-room/src/board/board-layout.css (77 lines), and it uses only the CSS system keywords canvas and highlight. className count across the app is 0 and there is no CSS-in-JS dependency.

Two tasks have already had to record contrast as explicitly NOT mechanically checkable because of this:
- task-4b274fad (Motion and colour-independence regression guards) excludes it in its DoD with this reason.
- task-667b1085 (Control-room journey gate) inherited real-browser contrast certification from task-ab8c9489 via governor comment comment-5dd36b5b, and cannot discharge it while no colour resolves.

This task closes that hole once, for both.

IMPORTANT — this is NOT a visual redesign, and epic scope forbids one. The app renders essentially unstyled today. The deliverable is a token layer that makes the EXISTING semantic tones resolve to concrete, AA-compliant values against a named background, in light and dark. Do not restyle surfaces, do not introduce a component library, and do not change any layout.

Owned paths: the token stylesheet and its test, plus the semanticTone-to-token mapping. Do NOT edit describeTruthClass's five descriptors: their glyph, shortLabel and borderStyle are pinned by CR-A11Y-001, which asserts the classes stay distinguishable with colour EXCLUDED.

Hard dependencies: none blocking.

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test
definitionOfDone: Every TruthSemanticTone prose value maps to a concrete foreground colour token and a named background token, in both light and dark. The mapping is exhaustive over the union and a test asserts exhaustiveness — adding a sixth tone without a token must fail the build or the test, never default silently.

A test computes the actual WCAG contrast ratio for every foreground/background token pair and asserts it meets AA (4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text and non-text indicators). It must assert the number of pairs checked is greater than zero and equals the number of declared tones, so a sweep over an empty or partial token set cannot pass.

The contrast computation is asserted against the production token values, not against a table restated inside the test. A test that recomputes its own expected colours proves only that the test is self-consistent.
A tone with no token, or a token that fails AA, produces a stable reason code naming the offending tone and ratio — the test asserts that specific code, not merely that something failed.

describeTruthClass's five descriptors are unchanged: glyph, shortLabel and borderStyle are untouched, and the committed CR-A11Y-001 monochrome check still passes, proving the classes remain distinguishable with colour excluded. Colour is added as a fourth channel, never as a replacement for the other three.

No layout, spacing or component structure changes. The only stylesheet edits are token declarations, every stylesheet carrying tokens also carries a @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block per the existing board-layout.css:68 pattern, and pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test passes.
taskRails: Pinned UI spec: D:/projexts/moes/docs/plans/2026-08-05-moe-v1-control-room-spec.md SHA-256 C55AF8A9FC7386E6492FD57E34A4B8321ABAAE4E4E08FF38703544B58B0BEF1F. Contrast is section 11.1 line 686; the truth-class tones are section 3.1; section 13.1 limits theming to light/dark plus monochrome survival and forbids visual tokens beyond section 3's semantics.

Colour is never the only carrier. Spec section 3.1 requires triple encoding — glyph, short label, colour — surviving monochrome, colour-vision deficiency and screen readers. This task adds the third channel; it must not weaken the first two. CR-A11Y-001 asserts the five classes stay distinguishable by glyph + label + border with colour EXCLUDED, and that test must still pass unchanged.

jsdom evaluates no CSS and document.styleSheets.length is 0 because Vitest stubs the CSS import (measured). Contrast must therefore be computed from the TOKEN VALUES as data — exported constants the stylesheet is generated from or pinned against — not by reading computed style from a rendered element. If the tokens live only as CSS text, the test must parse the real file and assert it parsed a non-zero number of declarations.

This is not a redesign. The app is deliberately near-unstyled and epic scope excludes visual redesign outside the pinned spec. Adding component styling, a design system, or a dependency is out of scope and will be rejected.
Split before 400 lines, target 250. Explicit owned paths only; no git add -A.

implementationPlan.description: Create apps/control-room/src/theme/wcag-contrast.ts: the contrast mathematics, as PRODUCTION code rather than a test helper. Export a function parsing a hex colour to linear RGB, a relative-luminance function per WCAG 2.x (channel/255, then c <= 0.03928 ? c/12.92 : ((c+0.055)/1.055)^2.4, then 0.2126R + 0.7152G + 0.0722B), and contrastRatio(foreground, background) = (lighter + 0.05) / (darker + 0.05). This lives in production and not in the test file for a specific reason the project rail names: a property must be asserted against the production surface, not against a test helper that reimplements it. A contrast function defined inside the test would only prove the test is self-consistent, which is exactly what DoD 3 forbids. Refuse a malformed colour string rather than returning a plausible number -- a silently wrong luminance produces a passing ratio for an unreadable pair, which is the worst possible failure here. Keep <=250 physical lines (`grep -c ''`).

Create apps/control-room/src/theme/truth-tone-tokens.ts: the token values and the certification, as the single source of truth. Declare the palette as `Record<TruthSemanticTone, {foreground, background}>` for light and again for dark, importing TruthSemanticTone from @moe/control-room-model. Using Record over the imported union is what makes DoD 1's exhaustiveness a COMPILE error rather than a runtime check: adding a sixth tone upstream fails the build here, and cannot default silently. Pick concrete hex values that clear AA against their named background -- 4.5:1 for normal text -- in both themes; the test in step 5 is the gate, so iterate values until it passes rather than guessing once. Expect "high-contrast magenta" and "amber" to be the two that need care: amber against a light background is the classic AA failure, and magenta must stay distinct from blue under both themes. Export a certifyToneTokens() that walks every tone in both themes, computes the ratio via wcag-contrast.ts, and returns either ok or a refusal carrying a stable code (e.g. TONE_CONTRAST_BELOW_AA) plus the offending tone name and the measured ratio, and a separate stable code for a tone with no token. DoD 4 requires the test to assert that specific code, so the code must be a production constant, not a thrown string.

Create apps/control-room/src/theme/truth-tone-tokens.css: CSS custom properties only. Declare one foreground and one background custom property per tone at :root for light, and repeat them inside a `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` block for dark, using the SAME values as the TypeScript palette. Attach the tones by the attribute the kernel already emits -- apps/control-room/src/kernel.tsx:109 renders `data-tone={descriptor.semanticTone}`, so `[data-tone="amber"] { color: var(--cr-tone-amber-fg); background: var(--cr-tone-amber-bg); }` needs no component change. Add a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block per DoD 6 and the board-layout.css:68 pattern, even though tokens declare no animation -- the DoD requires every token-carrying stylesheet to carry one. Declare NOTHING except custom properties and the per-tone colour rules: no spacing, no layout, no typography, no component selectors. Epic scope forbids a redesign and DoD 6 pins this to token declarations only.

Create apps/control-room/src/theme/truth-tone-tokens.test.ts. It must import the production palette and certifyToneTokens -- never restate a colour table (DoD 3). Assertions: (1) exhaustiveness -- the palette's key set equals the five tone values exactly, in both themes; (2) the contrast sweep -- iterate every foreground/background pair, assert each meets 4.5:1, AND assert the number of pairs checked is greater than zero and equals tones x themes (10), so a sweep over an empty or partial palette cannot pass silently, which DoD 2 requires explicitly and epic rail 6 requires generally; (3) the refusal path -- feed certifyToneTokens a deliberately failing palette and assert the exact stable code plus the offending tone name and measured ratio, not merely that it failed (DoD 4); (4) CSS/TS drift -- parse apps/control-room/src/theme/truth-tone-tokens.css as TEXT using the shell-narrow.test.tsx:17 pattern, assert every value in the TypeScript palette appears in the stylesheet, and assert the parsed declaration count is greater than zero so a renamed or emptied file cannot pass; (5) the reduced-motion block is present in the parsed text. Point 4 is the one that keeps the whole task honest: the TypeScript palette is what the test certifies, the stylesheet is what the browser renders, and nothing else stops them drifting apart.

Land the consumer edge: add the single side-effect line `import "./theme/truth-tone-tokens.css";` to apps/control-room/src/shell/frame.tsx, alongside its existing `import "./shell-layout.css";`. Without this the stylesheet is never loaded, the tokens never reach a browser, and the task ships a pure artifact that nothing imports -- Clause 1 requires a real consumer edge, and "the file exists" is not composition. SCOPE NOTE FOR QA: frame.tsx is outside the description's owned paths, which name the stylesheet, its test and the mapping. One side-effect import is included deliberately as the minimum possible consumer edge. It is not a layout, spacing or component-structure change, so DoD 6 holds: no element, class, or style rule in frame.tsx is touched. If a reviewer prefers the import live elsewhere, the requirement is only that exactly one module imports it once.

Mutation-drill the guards that can silently detach (epic rail 6). One at a time, mutate, re-run `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, confirm RED, restore exact bytes. Drill: (a) change one foreground value to a near-background shade -- the contrast assertion must redden and must name that tone and its ratio, proving DoD 4's code carries the offending tone rather than a generic failure; (b) delete one tone from the dark palette -- both the exhaustiveness assertion and the pair-count assertion must redden, proving the count guard is live and not decorative; (c) change one hex value in the .css file only, leaving TypeScript untouched -- the drift test must redden, which is the drill that proves the stylesheet and the certified palette cannot diverge; (d) empty the .css file -- the parsed-declaration-count guard must redden rather than the suite passing over zero declarations; (e) remove the reduced-motion block -- its assertion must redden. Then confirm the untouched-descriptor requirement of DoD 5 by running the committed CR-A11Y-001 check in apps/control-room/src/a11y/ui-wide-acceptance.test.tsx and confirming it passes UNCHANGED, and by `git diff -- packages/control-room-model/src/index.ts` returning empty. In this shared working directory a foreign completion hook can commit a drill edit while `git status` looks clean, so trust the red test and verify restoration with `git diff -- apps/control-room/` returning empty.

Adversarial review, then the gate. Review as an attacker: does any truth class now depend on colour to be distinguishable -- that is, did anything weaken glyph, shortLabel or borderStyle? Colour is the THIRD channel of a triple encoding and never a replacement, and if CR-A11Y-001 still passes unchanged that property holds. Did any layout, spacing, typography or component rule reach the stylesheet? Is any colour value present in the test that is not read from the production palette? Does the contrast function round or clamp in a way that could turn a 4.49 into a pass -- assert with a strict comparison against the AA threshold, not a tolerance. Confirm every new source is <=250 physical lines with `grep -c ''`. Then run the exact verification command `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` and paste fresh output as complete_task evidence; it is package-scoped, so no repo-wide attribution is needed, but if you also run a root leg and it is red, attribute by path per the baseline rail and disclose foreign red verbatim rather than claiming a green. Commit by explicit pathspec only after checking `git status --porcelain` for foreign staged entries: `git commit -- apps/control-room/src/theme/ apps/control-room/src/shell/frame.tsx`, then verify with `git show --stat` that only those paths landed.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
TYPESCRIPT AS SOURCE OF TRUTH, CSS PINNED AGAINST IT. The task rail permits either "exported constants the stylesheet is generated from or pinned against". I chose constants-plus-drift-test rather than generating the CSS, because generation would add a build step to a package that has none, and the drift test gives the same guarantee with less machinery. The crucial consequence is that DoD 3 is satisfied structurally: the test certifies the production palette it imports, and a separate assertion parses the real stylesheet to prove the two cannot diverge. Neither half restates a colour table.

CONTRAST MATH IN PRODUCTION, NOT IN THE TEST. Rejected: computing ratios inside the test file, which is the obvious place for it. The project rail is explicit that a property must be asserted against the production surface rather than a test helper that reimplements it, and a contrast function living in the test would prove only that the test agrees with itself. Putting it in wcag-contrast.ts also means the refusal in DoD 4 can carry a stable production code rather than a thrown string.

Record<TruthSemanticTone, Token> RATHER THAN A PLAIN OBJECT. This is what makes DoD 1's "adding a sixth tone without a token must fail the build or the test, never default silently" true at COMPILE time. A plain object plus a runtime key check would satisfy the letter of the DoD while letting a sixth tone reach a running app before anything complained.

THE CONSUMER EDGE, and the one scope expansion. The description's owned paths name the stylesheet, its test and the mapping -- not frame.tsx. But a stylesheet nothing imports never reaches a browser, and Clause 1 states that a pure artifact is not finished until one real consumer edge exists, with "exports the symbols" explicitly not counting. Step 6 therefore adds exactly one side-effect import line beside the existing `import "./shell-layout.css"`. That is the minimum possible edge and touches no element, class or rule, so DoD 6's "no layout, spacing or component structure changes" still holds. Flagged rather than smuggled.

ATTACHING BY data-tone RATHER THAN BY NEW CLASSNAMES. The kernel already emits data-tone on the chip, and the app has a className count of zero by design. Selecting on the existing attribute means the stylesheet attaches with no component change at all, which is what keeps this inside "not a redesign".

NOT TOUCHING describeTruthClass. Its five descriptors are pinned by CR-A11Y-001, which asserts distinguishability with colour EXCLUDED. This task adds colour as a fourth channel on top of glyph, shortLabel and borderStyle. If CR-A11Y-001 ever needed changing to accommodate this work, that would be the signal that the work had started replacing a channel instead of adding one.

planningNotes.risks:
1. THE PALETTE IS THE ONLY GENUINELY OPEN DESIGN CHOICE, and two tones are predictably hard. Amber on a light background is the classic AA failure -- a readable amber against white usually has to be dark enough to read as brown. "High-contrast magenta" must clear AA in BOTH themes while staying visually distinct from blue for a reader with a colour-vision deficiency. Expect to iterate values against the test rather than getting them right by inspection; the test is the gate, which is the point of building it first.

2. A SILENTLY WRONG LUMINANCE PASSES EVERYTHING. If the sRGB-to-linear step is wrong -- most often by skipping the 0.03928 branch or by applying the exponent to the raw 0-255 channel -- every ratio is wrong in the same direction and the suite goes green over unreadable pairs. Refuse malformed input rather than returning a plausible number, and sanity-check the function against a known pair (black on white is 21:1) before trusting any palette result.
